    # From the examples:
    # (10, -1) -> 9  (True)  => 10 + (-1) - 0 = 9
    # (0, 1) -> 1    (True)  => 0 + 1 - 0 = 1
    # (10, 1000) -> 1010 (True) => 10 + 1000 - 0 = 1010
    # (2, 0) -> 2    (True)  => 2 + 0 - 0 = 2
    # (-10, 1) -> -9 (True)  => -10 + 1 - 0 = -9
    # (-99, -10) -> -109 (True) => -99 + (-10) - 0 = -109

    # The false cases:
    # (-10, -1000) -> -1009 (False) but -10 + (-1000) = -1010, so output is -1009, which is off by +1
    # (-99, 1) -> -97 (False) but -99 + 1 = -98, output is -97, off by +1
    # (0, -99) -> -97 (False) but 0 + (-99) = -99, output is -97, off by +2
    # (1, -10) -> -7 (False) but 1 + (-10) = -9, output is -7, off by +2
    # (2, 1) -> 13 (False) but 2 + 1 = 3, output is 13, off by +10
    # (0, 1000) -> 999 (False) but 0 + 1000 = 1000, output is 999, off by -1

    # All True outputs match a + b exactly.
    # So the function is simply sum of a and b.

    return a + b
